note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 67, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Exact linked article, named engagement and complete source first/last day match the catalogue. The row is parentless, with no competing source row for this target. Preserve the two original source NAM force identities; counts remain CDB estimates.

The recorded Prussian army receives a musket-bearing infantry analogy supported by a surviving Model 1740 weapon and the 1750 infantry dress regulation. This review uses the latter only for battles after 1750; grenadier caps, cavalry and artillery are not generalized from it. The model is a representative infantry component, not an exact regimental uniform or a statement that every soldier used that equipment. Coalition identities, component proportions, CDB 90 personnel evidence and all loss categories remain unchanged.

Equipment review (Kolin, 1757): preserve the CDB90 AUS ARMY aggregate. A white-coat fusilier with a tricorne, black gaiters and a long flintlock with socket bayonet represents one regular infantry component. The coat uses the 1762 Ligne portrait as a visual analogy; its rose facings do not establish the regiments present or their proportions. The M1754 service reference and photographed firearm support the weapon family, not universal issue or an exact mechanical reconstruction. Grenadiers, Hungarian and frontier dress, cavalry, artillery and allied contingents are not individually reconstructed. The model is limited to 1756–1763 and is not carried into the 1767 Kaskett period. Identity evidence is separate from equipment evidence; no quantities, camps or dates are changed.
